title: Question 1.1
statement_text: Given a graph class $\mathcal{G}$, is there a constant $c_{\mathcal{G}}$ such that $$\frac{\gamma(G)}{\rho(G)}\leqslant c_{\mathcal{G}}\quad\text{ for each }\quad G\in\mathcal{G}~{}~{}?$$
context_text: The dominating number $\gamma(G)$ is the minimum size of a set of vertices whose closed neighborhoods cover $V(G)$; the packing number $\rho(G)$ is the maximum size of a set of vertices whose closed neighborhoods are pairwise disjoint (equivalently, pairwise at distance at least $3$). Always $\gamma(G)\ge\rho(G)$, and $\gamma(G)\le\Delta(G)\rho(G)$. The two parameters are optima of integer programs whose linear relaxations are dual, so a constant bound on $\gamma/\rho$ bounds the integrality gap of both programs. Known bounded classes include $K_{q,r}$-minor-free graphs, graphs of bounded Euler genus, classes of bounded weak colouring number $\mathrm{wcol}_2$, and bounded twin-width; the authors prove bounds $\gamma\le7\rho$ for $2$-degenerate graphs, $\gamma\le3\rho$ for AT-free graphs, $\gamma\le32\rho$ for unit-disk graphs, $\gamma\le k\rho$ for treewidth at most $k$, $\gamma\le10\rho$ for planar graphs and $\gamma\le4k^2\rho$ for twin-width at most $k$. On the other hand the ratio is unbounded for Cartesian products $K_n\square K_n$ ($\gamma=n$, $\rho=1$), for split graphs (hence chordal graphs) and for $3$-degenerate graphs (which also gives classes of bounded VC-dimension with unbounded ratio). The question is asked for each class $\mathcal{G}$ separately; it remains open e.g. for homogeneously orderable graphs, chordal bipartite graphs, and intersection graphs of axis-parallel rectangles in the plane or boxes in $\mathbb{R}^3$. For subcubic connected graphs, Henning et al. conjectured $\gamma\le2\rho+1$.
paper_title: On graph classes with constant domination-packing ratio

title: Conjecture 1.2 (Henning, Löwenstein, and Rautenbach)
statement_text: Let $G$ be a connected graph with $\Delta(G)\leqslant 3$, then $\gamma(G)\leqslant 2\rho(G)+1$. The equality holds only for three well-defined graphs, one of which being the Petersen graph.
context_text: Henning, Löwenstein, and Rautenbach showed that if $\Delta(G)\leqslant 2$ then $\gamma(G)\leqslant\rho(G)+1$, and that if $G$ is claw-free with $\Delta(G)\leqslant 3$ then $\gamma(G)\leqslant 2\rho(G)$. They then stated this conjecture for general subcubic graphs. The general upper bound $\gamma(G)\leqslant\Delta(G)\rho(G)$ serves as the trivial baseline.
paper_contribution: The paper sharpens Conjecture 1.2, improving related constants and providing new structural context through results on 2-degenerate graphs and other graph classes.
paper_title: On graph classes with constant domination-packing ratio

title: Question 9.1
statement_text: Characterize those graph classes $\mathcal{G}$ for which there is a constant $c_{\mathcal{G}}$ such that $\dfrac{\gamma(G)}{\rho(G)}\leqslant c_{\mathcal{G}}$ for each $G\in\mathcal{G}$.
context_text: The dominating number $\gamma(G)$ is the minimum size of a set of vertices whose closed neighborhoods cover $V(G)$; the packing number $\rho(G)$ is the maximum size of a set of vertices whose closed neighborhoods are pairwise disjoint (equivalently, pairwise at distance at least $3$). Always $\gamma(G)\ge\rho(G)$, and $\gamma(G)\le\Delta(G)\rho(G)$. The two parameters are optima of integer programs whose linear relaxations are dual, so a constant bound on $\gamma/\rho$ bounds the integrality gap of both programs. Known bounded classes include $K_{q,r}$-minor-free graphs, graphs of bounded Euler genus, classes of bounded weak colouring number $\mathrm{wcol}_2$, and bounded twin-width; the authors prove bounds $\gamma\le7\rho$ for $2$-degenerate graphs, $\gamma\le3\rho$ for AT-free graphs, $\gamma\le32\rho$ for unit-disk graphs, $\gamma\le k\rho$ for treewidth at most $k$, $\gamma\le10\rho$ for planar graphs and $\gamma\le4k^2\rho$ for twin-width at most $k$. On the other hand the ratio is unbounded for Cartesian products $K_n\square K_n$ ($\gamma=n$, $\rho=1$), for split graphs (hence chordal graphs) and for $3$-degenerate graphs (which also gives classes of bounded VC-dimension with unbounded ratio). Since $2$-degenerate graphs, which are not sparse in the sense of bounded weak colouring numbers (they contain all $1$-subdivisions of graphs), have bounded ratio while $3$-degenerate graphs do not, no characterization purely in terms of sparsity is possible, although previous results had suggested that sparsity (e.g. bounded weak colouring numbers) might be the key property. The authors call this a major open problem.
